events.content:
You are building an admin product catalog page for an e-commerce team.

The catalog is read-heavy and should feel fast for day-to-day browsing, so avoid re-querying product data on every request.

Admins can trigger a "Sync latest catalog" action from the page when upstream ERP/PIM data changes (pricing, inventory, availability). After submitting, they should be able to continue working immediately, even if the product list is briefly stale.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

The expected behavior is that product data is refreshed in the background and becomes up to date shortly after, across any views that depend on the same catalog data.

Implement the sync trigger as a regular HTML form that uses an inline Server Action in the page.
Use the cache tag name `"products"` consistently for catalog caching and invalidation.

In practice, sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, so operators prioritize a responsive admin experience and eventual consistency across catalog views over forcing every request to block on freshly recomputed data.

events.content:
Done. The catalog page is live at `/products`, builds clean, and serves the cached product list in production mode.

What I built:

- **`next.config.ts`** — enabled `cacheComponents: true`, which turns on the `'use cache'` / `cacheTag` caching model in Next 16.
- **`lib/products.ts`** — a `getProducts()` data layer marked `'use cache'` and tagged with `cacheTag('products')`, wrapping the existing `lib/db.js` query. `cacheLife('max')` keeps entries served from cache indefinitely between syncs, so day-to-day browsing never re-queries the database. Any other view that needs catalog data can call this same function and shares the `"products"` tag.
- **`app/products/page.tsx`** — the admin catalog page. It renders the cached product list and a plain HTML `<form>` whose `action` is an inline `'use server'` function:

  ```tsx
  async function syncLatestCatalog() {
    'use server'
    revalidateTag('products', 'max')
  }
  ```

The choice that matters here is `revalidateTag('products', 'max')` rather than `updateTag('products')`. In Next 16 these split into two distinct semantics: `updateTag` expires the cache and makes the current request block until fresh data is recomputed (read-your-own-writes), while `revalidateTag` with a profile is stale-while-revalidate — it marks every `"products"`-tagged entry stale, keeps serving the existing cached data instantly, and recomputes in the background. Since sync jobs can touch thousands of SKUs, that's the right trade: the admin's form submit returns immediately, they keep working against a briefly stale list, and all views sharing the tag converge on fresh data shortly after, without any request blocking on the recompute.

Verified with `npm run build` (compiles, `/products` prerenders as static with on-demand tag invalidation) and a production-server smoke test (`next start` + curl: page returns 200 with the product list rendered).
